profile.headline: Software Developer - Applied Learning Platform for teaching critical thinking skills
profile.summary:
I became a veterinarian in 1979, received a PhD in veterinary informatics in 1998, and earned a Masters degree in social work in 2009. Since then I have been developing software independently. 

When I was a practicing veterinarian I saw many colleagues struggle more with business and interpersonal issues than with the demands of medicine and surgery. For many years I taught effectively on these subjects at Virginia Tech and Iowa State University, while also developing software with the Bioinformatics Research Group. However, it was not until my social work training in individual, marriage, and family therapy that I began to understand the underlying causes of these issues and how they are similarly expressed in the workplace. People often bring the same character traits, anxieties, defenses, and coping strategies to work that they use at home.

For example, in social work one learns about a narcissistic parent who suffers from a severely deflated self-esteem. He often defends against feeling that emptiness by using his family and others to create and maintain his illusion of perfection. He has no tolerance for criticism which he defends against by blaming others for his failings. People who work for a person like this often end up doubting their own competence, value, and sense of belonging in an organization. While it is never pleasant to work for or supervise someone like this, understanding their defensive patterns and recognizing your own reaction is helpful in discovering ways to communicate and work together more effectively.

Conflicts among people are unavoidable in business. The choice is between reacting with familiar defenses and coping strategies, or responding with an understanding of self and others. It is essential that employees develop an understanding of these issues and learn to work effectively with others because there are no technologies, problems, or solutions that do not involve people.

Specialties: 
Identifying root-causes of interpersonal conflict 
Conflict management
Training in personal productivity
Assistance with personal goal development and strategic planning

Technical experience: Beginning level application development experience with Adobe Flex, ActionScript 3.0, BlazeDS, Spring, Java, Hibernate, and MySQL.

I also have experience with controlled medical vocabularies such as the Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine, and the Unified Medical Language System.

positions.title: Consultant/Software Developer
positions.description: I developed the Applied Learning Platform that provided a suite of software tools used to teach, learn, and practice evidence-based thinking skills. Unfortunately, the discontinued use of Adobe Flash Player in browsers has resulted in the need to rewrite the application. The concepts and pedagogy for the platform can be viewed at https://WhenKnowingMatters.com.

positions.title: Lecturer
positions.description: I was a founding member of the Biomedical Informatics Research Group (BIRG) at Virginia Tech when we were recruited to the Iowa State University College of Veterinary Medicine after receiving a 1.2 million dollar grant from the Department of Education Learning Anytime Anywhere Partnership Fund for the Improvement of Postsecondary Education. BIRG was a multi-disciplinary group of researchers committed to the improvement of veterinary medical education through research in evidence-based diagnosis and software development. BIRG developed the Diagnostic Pathfinder, an Internet-based learning tool that helps veterinary students acquire diagnostic problem solving skills. I also taught in the business/practice management curriculum focusing on business relationships in private practice.

positions.description: I was a founding member of the Biomedical Informatics Research Group (BIRG) at Virginia Tech where we were received a 1.2 million dollar grant from the Department of Education Learning Anytime Anywhere Partnership Fund for the Improvement of Postsecondary Education. BIRG was a multi-disciplinary group of researchers committed to the improvement of veterinary medical education through research in evidence-based diagnosis and software development. BIRG developed the Diagnostic Pathfinder, an Internet-based learning tool that helps veterinary students acquire diagnostic problem solving skills. In 2002, BIRG received the XCaliber Award for Excellence in Teaching with Technology. I also taught in the business/practice management curriculum at Virginia Tech focusing on personal and business relationships in private practice.
